The Theory of Becoming · the map · as a page · the laws, tie by tie · every dynamic · every case

One map of what goes on, and what holds between

How anything forms, lasts, changes and ends, drawn on one web: eleven kinds of role and the ties between them. A law is a theorem, proved in Lean on a stated model: it says something general about one tie or one role. A case is one test, in its own words, with what in it was taken as which role. The two are kept apart, and the map shows where they have met.

Where reasoning has met a case

A law says: if these hold, then that. A frozen prediction is written down before its test is run and names the laws or the thesis it rests on; its test's record then says which of its conditions were met and what was seen. Of 295 frozen predictions, 154 rest on a law or a thesis and could have come out either way: 69 follow from a law under its bridge, 66 say more than any law, 19 are forecasts. Each is placed here by its own record. Counted apart: 26 checks that name a law or a thesis, 115 frozen entries that name neither, and 18 entries their records state without a freeze.

What holds of anything that goes on

23 dynamics name no role: they hold of every course or every process. They are the map's legend: what staying, leaving and returning mean.

Every law is a theorem about a stated model, checked in Lean; its sentence here is in the kinds' words and its model's own terms, and its conditions are premises the atlas's ledger lists for it. Read a law with its conditions. A case cannot make a proved law wrong: it falls under the law or outside it. What a case can show wrong is the pairing of its things with the roles (a bridge), a measure, a scoring rule or a thesis. Roles of two models are drawn as one place where each model names that kind of role; where no proof joins the two models, that sameness is a reading. AI-written, 11 November 2026: each card from the Lean statements and each case from its experiment's own record, each put to a second reader to refute. The map adds no result.
